_about: Everything villagers say. 'gift_lines' are what they say to a gift they don't love (by villager, then item); anything missing gets a polite thank-you. {sweater} = Rosa's sweater price today, {cottage} = cottage price, {rent} = cottage rent. 'lines' has three tiers per villager: 0-1 hearts, 2-3 hearts, 4-5 hearts.

intro.rosa: Oh, a new face! I'm Rosa, I run the market stall. Bring me your sweaters. When the market's good I pay better than that old shipping bin. Today it's {sweater}c each.
intro.theo: Welcome to the Yarn Barn! I'm Theo. Wool, yarn, and the occasional sheep. If your flock needs a new friend, I've got a few ewes out back.
intro.mabel: Mabel Finch, Willow Homes. Looking to put down roots? Rosewood Cottage, just south of the plaza, is for sale. {cottage} coins and it's yours.
intro.rowan: Rowan. I keep the flock on the hill past your place. If you hear bleating at dawn, that's mine. Probably.
intro.hazel: Mind the flour, it gets everywhere. I'm Hazel. If it's warm and it came out of that oven, I made it. Croissants are best before nine and gone by ten.
intro.wren: Wren. Mayor, for my sins, and chief welcomer. If anything in Maple Grove is broken, it's probably on my list. If it isn't on my list, tell me and it will be.
intro.pip: Pip, post. If it's got a stamp on it, it's been through these hands. I know everyone's business and I tell nobody. Mostly.
intro.gus: Gus. Builder's Delight. Timber, nails, hinges, mugs, mousetraps. If your house needs it, I've got it, or I know a man. I am the man.

rosa: Sweaters are going for {sweater}c today. Prices change every morning, so check the board.
The tourists from the city go wild for anything hand-knit.
If you ever grow pumpkins, save one for me. I make a mean pie.
You're becoming my favorite supplier! I pay you a little extra now: {sweater}c a sweater today.
Theo says your wool is the softest in the valley. Don't tell him I agreed.
I put one of your sweaters on display. Three people asked who made it!
Between us, I tell customers your sweaters are 'Birchfield originals.' They pay more for the name!
My late husband would have loved your farm. He always said the best things are made slowly.
You've got a real knitting empire going, dear. {sweater}c a sweater, just for you.
theo: Out of wool? I sell it in bundles of three. Just enough for one sweater.
A happy sheep grows better wool. Pet them every day. That's science. Probably.
I'm learning cable knits. My scarf currently looks like a pretzel.
I knock a little off my prices for friends. You count.
A single sheep grows enough wool for six sweaters a year. Wild, right?
Rosa pretends she doesn't like my jokes. She laughs on the inside.
You inspired me. I'm entering the Harvest Knit-Off this year!
If you ever open a shop in town, I'd put your sweaters in my window. Free of charge.
Best customer, best neighbor. Don't let it go to your head.
mabel: Real estate is simple: make a place cozy, and people will pay to live there.
Every piece of furniture in a rental raises the rent. People pay for cozy.
Rosewood Cottage has the best garden light in Maple Grove. I'd know.
You've got a good eye. I'll take a little off the price of any property for you.
Turnip stew reminds me of my grandmother's kitchen. Funny what sticks with you.
There's talk of new lots opening up north of town next season. Keep your coins handy.
You're my favorite client. Don't tell the mayor.
One day this whole valley will be wearing your sweaters and renting your houses.
Keep this up and they'll name a street after you.
rowan: Your fence on the east side leans. I'd fix it before the ewes notice.
Weather's turning. Sheep always know first.
Most folks who move out here from the city last a season. You've got a look like you might stay.
You've got wool on your sleeve. Suits you.
I walked past your place last night. Light was on late. Knitting, or not sleeping?
Theo won't stop talking about your work. Takes a lot to get Theo talking. Well. Less than you'd think.
I used to hate quiet evenings. Lately I don't mind them.
If you ever want to see the hill at sunset, I know the best rock to sit on.
You don't have to tell me what you left behind. But I'd listen, if you wanted.
hazel: Cold butter, warm kitchen, up at four. That's the whole secret. Mostly the up-at-four part.
Theo buys a bun every morning and says it's for the sheep. The sheep never see that bun.
You look hungry. Everyone who walks in here looks hungry. That's the smell doing its job.
I've started saving you the corner pieces. Don't tell anyone or they'll all want corners.
Your gran liked her loaf dark. 'Burn it a little, Hazel.' I still bake one her way on Sundays.
Mabel pays in exact change. Every single time. I've never once seen that woman get change.
If you ever want to learn the croissants, come by at four. I'll have the kettle on.
I'm making a sheep-shaped loaf for the harvest fair. It looks like a cloud with legs. It's perfect.
Best part of my morning is the bell going and it being you.
wren: The fountain's been leaking since spring. It's on the list. Everything's on the list.
We had a town meeting about the bench by the bakery. Three hours. The bench is fine.
Your gran ran the harvest fair for twenty years. Nobody's dared take it over.
People are talking about you. Nicely, for once. You've made a good start.
If you need a hand with anything at the farm, say the word. I'm terrible with a hammer, but I know who isn't.
I've put 'help Nora settle in' at the top of my list. It's the only thing on it I enjoy.
Maple Grove's lucky to have you. I'd say it at the fair, but you'd go red.
Your gran would be proud. She'd never have said so, mind. She'd have knitted you something instead.
Some mornings I walk past your farm just to see the smoke from the chimney. Feels like the town's whole again.
pip: Nothing for you today. Nothing's good news, I always say.
Mabel gets a seed catalogue every week. Every week. Same catalogue.
Rain or shine, the post gets through. Mostly shine round here, thank goodness.
Your gran used to leave a biscuit on the gatepost for me. Just saying.
I'm not saying who, but somebody in this town gets letters with hearts on.
My knees know every cobble in the plaza by name.
If a letter comes for you from the city, I'll bring it round myself. Not leave it in the box.
Best part of my round is the bit past your farm. It smells like hay and woodsmoke.
You've settled in like you were always here. The post can tell.
gus: Measure twice, cut once. Or measure once and come back to me for more wood. Either's good for business.
Hinges, nails and string. Most of life's problems, sorted.
Your gran bought the same broom off me every five years and complained about the last one each time.
How's that pen holding up? Sheep lean. They're always leaning.
I've got a lovely bit of oak out back. Not for sale. I just like looking at it.
Theo says yarn's the backbone of this town. I say it's the fence posts. We've been arguing for eleven years.
You build like your gran knitted. Bit crooked, all heart.
If you ever want a workbench at the farm, I'll give you mates' rates.
Pull up a crate. Nobody's in a hurry in here.

rosa.sweater: For me? Oh, you'll make me cry on the stall and then nobody buys anything.
rosa.turnip: A good firm turnip. You know the way to a market woman's heart: produce.

theo.pumpkin: A pumpkin! I'll carve a sheep into it. It'll look like a potato. It'll be perfect.
theo.turnip: Turnip. Right. Thank you. I'm sure the sheep will love it.

mabel.sweater: Hand-knit! I'll wear it to the next viewing and tell everyone it's local.
mabel.pumpkin: Lovely. I'll put it on the office step. Makes the place look settled.

rowan.pumpkin: Soup, then. I'll make it badly and eat it anyway. Thanks.
rowan.turnip: A turnip. ... The ewes will think I've gone soft. Thank you.

hazel.turnip: A turnip! That's soup. Thank you, love. It'll be on the counter by lunch.
hazel.sweater: For me? It's so soft. I'm keeping it well away from the flour.

gift_loved.rosa: A pumpkin! Oh, you remembered. I'm baking a pie tonight and you're getting the first slice.
gift_loved.theo: Is this... one of YOUR sweaters? For me? I'm wearing it every day. Every single day.
gift_loved.mabel: Turnips! Just like my grandmother grew. You've made an old realtor very happy.
gift_loved.rowan: You made this. For me. ... I don't really know what to say. Thank you. I'll wear it up on the hill.
gift_loved.hazel: Pumpkin! Bread, scones, soup, a pie for the window... Come back tomorrow, there'll be something in it for you.
gift_loved.wren: For me? Oh, this is beautiful. I'm wearing it to the next town meeting, and I'm telling everyone who made it.
gift_loved.pip: A turnip! You remembered. Nobody remembers. That's going in tonight's stew.
gift_loved.gus: Now that's a pumpkin. I'll put it on the counter. Best-looking thing in the shop.
